title: Question: finite families yielding clean H-free classes
statement_text: For which finite families $\mathcal{H}$ of graphs is the class of all $\mathcal{H}$-free graphs clean?
context_text: A graph is $\mathcal{H}$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal{H}$. For a positive integer $t$, the $t$-basic obstructions are the complete graph $K_t$, the complete bipartite graph $K_{t,t}$, all subdivisions of the $(t\times t)$-wall $W_{t\times t}$ (the standard subcubic planar grid-like graph whose subdivisions are used in grid-minor theorems), and the line graphs of all subdivisions of $W_{t\times t}$; a graph is $t$-clean if it contains no $t$-basic obstruction as an induced subgraph, and a class $\mathcal{C}$ is clean if for every $t$ there is $w(t)$ such that every $t$-clean graph in $\mathcal{C}$ has treewidth at most $w(t)$. A subdivided star forest is a forest in which every component has at most one vertex of degree more than two. The class of all graphs is not clean, while proper minor-closed classes, classes of bounded maximum degree (Korhonen) and graphs with no long hole are clean. The authors prove that the class of $H$-free graphs is clean if and only if $H$ is a subdivided star forest; a characterization of all families $\mathcal{H}$ giving clean classes would amount to a full grid-type theorem for induced subgraphs, which is out of reach, so finite families are the natural next step. Any finite $\mathcal{H}$ containing a subdivided star forest yields a clean class, but the converse fails: if $H$ is the unique double star on six vertices (two adjacent vertices of degree 3, the smallest tree that is not a subdivided star), then $\{H,K_3\}$-free graphs form a clean class. The authors announce that an upcoming paper by four of them gives a full description of the finite families $\mathcal{H}$ for which the class of $\mathcal{H}$-free graphs is clean.
